Sharp played [[college basketball]] for the [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston Cougars]], with whom in 2026 he was named [[List of All-Big 12 Conference men's basketball teams|First-team All-Big 12]] and to the Big 12 All-Defensive Team. He was drafted by the Kings in the second round of the [[2026 NBA draft]], ==Early life == Sharp was born and raised in [[Tel Aviv]], Israel.[https://www.jpost.com/international/article-900618 "Israeli-American Emanuel Sharp, son of Maccabi TA legend Derrick Sharp, gets drafted to the NBA,"] The Jerusalem Post, June 26, 2026. His father is naturalized Israeli and former [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] basketball guard and captain [[Derrick Sharp]].[https://www.ynetnews.com/article/c7gu1q7hj "NBA: Emanuel Sharp, son of former Maccabi Tel Aviv captain, drafted by Sacramento,"] ynet, June 24, 2026.[https://www.timesofisrael.com/nbas-sacramento-kings-draft-tel-aviv-born-emanuel-sharp/ "NBA’s Sacramento Kings draft Tel Aviv-born Emanuel Sharp,"] Times of Israel, June 26, 2026. Derrick Sharp played college ball at the [[South Florida Bulls men's basketball|University of South Florida]], where he averaged 15.1 points, 3.1 assists, and 1.1 steals per game while shooting 38.6% from three-point range and 82.5% from the free throw line.[https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/derrick-sharp-1.html "Derrick Sharp ,"], Sports-reference.{{cite web | title=Who Are Emanuel Sharp's Parents? Exploring the Family Behind the Rising Basketball Star | website=College Sports Network | date=2025-04-02 | url=https://collegefootballnetwork.com/mens-college-basketball/who-emanuel-sharp-parents-family-behind-rising-star/ | access-date=2026-07-11}} He then played his entire professional career in Israel, mostly with Maccabi Tel Aviv (for 15 years, from 1996 to 2011), helped them win the [[2000–01 FIBA SuproLeague|2001 FIBA SuproLeague title]] and two [[EuroLeague]] titles, and was subsequently the assistant coach of the team from 2011 to 2013 under [[David Blatt]].[https://www.fiba.basketball/en/news/europe-u16-2019-news-all-in-the-family-for-bagatskis-radja-sharp-and-boskovic "All in the family for Bagatskis, Radja, Sharp and Boskovic,"] FIBA Basketball, August 10, 2019.[https://jhvonline.com/israeli-citizen-playing-key-role-in-uh-mens-basketball-success-p34561-256.htm "Israeli citizen playing key role in UH men’s basketball success,"] ''Jewish Herald-Voice'', February 20, 2025. Emanuel's Canadian-born mother Justine Ellison Sharp played basketball for the [[Toronto Varsity Blues|University of Toronto]], led the team to two national silver medals, was named the women's 1996 university athlete of the year in her senior season, and was inducted into the school's Varsity Blues hall of fame in 2009.[https://www.sportsnet.ca/ncaa-mens-basketball/article/houston-star-with-canadian-ties-named-big-12-tournaments-top-player/ "Houston star with Canadian ties named Big 12 Tournament's top player,"] March 15, 2025, sportsnet.ca. She went on to play professional basketball in Israel for a decade, and obtained Israeli citizenship upon marrying Derrick Sharp.[https://www.legalimmigrationisrael.com/blog/citizenship-for-mixed-heritage-israelis/ "Citizenship for Mixed-Heritage Israelis: Deni Avdija and Others,"] legalimmigrationisrael.com, June 22, 2025. Emanuel has three brothers, Gabriel (who played college basketball at [[Kalamazoo Hornets|Kalamazoo College]]), Noah, and Derrick Jr. (who plays pro basketball in Israel, and lives in [[Haifa]]), and a sister named Maya.[https://uhcougars.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/emanuel-sharp/9540 "Emanuel Sharp - Men's Basketball,"] University of Houston Athletics.[https://www.papercitymag.com/culture/emanuel-sharp-houston-brother-dj-sharp-deals-war-israel-ncaa-tournament/ "War and Basketball — Houston’s Emanuel Sharp Plays In the NCAA Tournament As His Brother Deals With Much More In Israel, With Rockets, Fear & 3:30 AM Tipoffs,"] PaperCity, March 22, 2024. ==High school== He was coached by his father in high school. As a sophomore in 2019-20, Sharp was Florida's fourth-leading scorer with 31.9 points per game at [[Howard W. Blake High School|Blake High School]] in [[Tampa, Florida]], and was named Florida Class 5A State Player of the Year. As a junior in 2020-21, he averaged 24.7 points, 3.9 assists, 2.6 rebounds, and 1.8 steals a game for [[Bishop McLaughlin Catholic High School]], where he played alongside fellow future NBA draft pick [[Dillon Mitchell (basketball)|Dillon Mitchell]], and was named Florida Class 3A Player of the Year, and named to the ''[[Suncoast News]]'' All-County Team.{{cite web |url=https://www.tampabaybeacons.com/2026/06/25/one-team-two-roads-same-draft-night/ |title=One team, two roads, same draft night |last=Putnam |first=Bob |publisher=Tampa Bay Beacons |date=June 25, 2026 |access-date=June 30, 2026}}[https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/college/article/Kelvin-Sampson-Emanuel-Sharp-rehab-from-injury-17004177.php "'It breaks my heart': UH's Emanuel Sharp reflects on career cut short by Sweet 16 loss to Illinois,"] Houston Chronicle, March 27, 2026. He did not compete as a senior in 2021-22, as he was recovering from a severe injury in which he broke his [[fibula]] and [[Joint dislocation|dislocated his ankle]] in a [[pickup game]] in May 2021; it took 18 months for him to recover from the injury.[https://dailyorange.com/2025/11/syracuse-mens-basketball-emanuel-sharp-houston-never-quit/ "Houston didn’t quit on Emanuel Sharp. Now, he wants to bring it a championship,"] The Daily Orange, December 2025. [[ESPN]] ranked Sharp the number 60 player nationally and the number 11 [[shooting guard]] nationally (he was ranked number 18 nationally by [[247Sports]], and number 20 by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]]), and he was considered a [[4-star recruit]] by ESPN, 247Sports, and Rivals. Coming out of high school, Sharp committed to play [[college basketball]] for the [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston Cougars]]. He picked the team over other schools such as Texas Tech, Florida, Louisville, Georgia Tech, Rutgers, Arizona, Clemson, Penn State, SMU, Iona, and USF.{{cite web |last1=Duarte |first1=Joseph |title=UH picks up commitment from shooting guard Emanuel Sharp |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/college/article/UH-picks-up-commitment-from-shooting-guard-16175858.php |website=Houston Chronicle |date=13 May 2021 |access-date=23 March 2025}} ==College career== As a [[freshman]] in 2021–22 at the University of Houston, where he majored in integrated studies, Sharp was [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]].{{cite web |last1=Duarte |first1=Joseph |date=February 3, 2025 |title=Why UH coach Kelvin Sampson thinks it's best to rest Emanuel Sharp for two games |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/college/article/uh-basketball-emanuel-sharp-ankle-injury-20136145.php |access-date=23 March 2025 |website=Houston Chronicle}} As a redshirt freshman in 2022–23, he averaged 15.6 minutes, 5.9 points, and 2.2 rebounds per game while shooting 88.1% from the free throw line in 33 games off the bench.{{cite web |title=Emanuel Sharp 2022-23 Game Logs |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/emanuel-sharp-1/gamelog/2023 |website=Sports Reference |access-date=23 March 2025}} He was named to the 2022-23 [[American Conference (NCAA)|AAC]] All-Freshman team. During his 2023–24 sophomore season, Sharp averaged 12.6 points, 3.5 rebounds, and 1.5 steals (9th in the conference) per game while shooting 46.8% from three-point range (6th) and 85.1% from the free throw line (6th) in all of the team's 37 games (32 of which he started).[https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/emanuel-sharp-1.html "Emanuel Sharp,"] sports-reference.com .{{cite web |last1=Albergio |first1=Camryn |title=Breaking down Houston men’s basketball 2024-25 roster |url=https://thedailycougar.com/2024/11/04/breaking-down-houston-mens-basketball-2024-25-roster/ |website=The Daily Cougar |access-date=23 March 2025}} In the second round of the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]], Sharp led the way with 30 points and seven threes in a win over [[2023–24 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Texas A&M]].{{cite web |last1=Duarte |first1=Joseph |title=How Houston's Emanuel Sharp became known as 'Crash' |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/college/article/uh-basketball-emanuel-sharp-duke-19365912.php |website=Houston Chronicle |access-date=23 March 2025}} On November 22, 2024, Sharp hit five threes in a win over [[2024–25 Hofstra Pride men's basketball team|Hofstra]].{{cite web |last1=Duarte |first1=Joseph |title=UH's Emanuel Sharp leads the nation in 3-point accuracy thanks to 'confidence' and consistent form |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/college/article/uh-basketball-emanuel-sharp-3-point-shooting-20030808.php |website=Houston Chronicle |access-date=23 March 2025}} On November 30, he put up 23 points in an overtime loss to [[2024–25 San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball team|San Diego State]]. On January 25, 2025 Sharp scored eight points in a double overtime victory against [[2024–25 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]].{{cite web |last1=Ringgold |first1=Buck |title=Kelvin Sampson to hold out Houston guard Emanuel Sharp this week due to injury |url=https://www.si.com/college/houston/basketball/kelvin-sampson-to-hold-out-houston-guard-emanuel-sharp-this-week-due-to-injury-01jk748k5xvj |work=Houston Cougars on SI |publisher=SI.com |access-date=23 March 2025}} On February 18, he notched 17 points with four threes in a victory versus [[2024–25 Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball team|Arizona State]].{{cite web |last1=Duarte |first1=Joseph |title=How UH's Emanuel Sharp went from 'out of whack' to getting his 3-point groove back |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/college/article/uh-basketball-emanuel-sharp-rebounds-20175160.php |website=Houston Chronicle |access-date=23 March 2025}} During the [[2025 Big 12 men's basketball tournament]] and NCAA Midwest Regional, Sharp helped lead his team to a conference title, where he was named the tournament's Most Outstanding Player.{{cite web |last1=Baldwin |first1=Chris |title=Emanuel Sharp Is Finally Feeling Healthy, Lifting NCAA Tournament No. 1 Seed Houston’s Special March Potential Even Higher |url=https://www.papercitymag.com/culture/emanuel-sharp-healthy-one-seed-houston-big-12-tournament-most-outstanding-player/ |website=PaperCity Magazine |access-date=23 March 2025}} In the March Madness tournament, Sharp and the Cougars would reach the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|championship game]], where they fell short at the buzzer against [[2024-25 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]], with the final score being 65–63. During the 2024–25 season, he averaged 12.6 points, 3.0 rebounds, and 1.4 steals per game while shooting 40.7% from three-point range and 86.8% from the free throw line (4th in the conference) in 37 games (36 of which he started). Sharp was named the 2025 Big 12 Tournament MVP, the 2025 NCAA Tournament Midwest Regional Most Outstanding Player, and to the 2025 All-Big 12 Tournament team, the 2025 NCAA Tournament All-Region team, and the 2025 Winter All-Big 12 Academic Team. During his 2025–26 senior season, Sharp averaged 15.5 points, 3.0 rebounds, 1.7 assists, and 1.2 steals per game while shooting 37.2% from three-point range (6th in the conference) and a [[Big 12 Conference]]-leading 89.1% from the free throw line in 37 games (all of which he started). He was named to the 2025-26 All-Big 12 - 1st Team, and the 2025-26 Big 12 All-Defense team. His career 87.0% free throw shooting percentage is third all-time in the Big 12 Conference.[https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/conferences/big-12/men/leaders/ft-pct-player-career.html "Men's Big 12 Conference Career Free Throw Percentage Leaders, "] sports-reference.com. Sharp also set the Cougars' record for career three-pointers, with 309. ==Professional career== On June 24, 2026, Sharp was selected by the [[Sacramento Kings]] with the 45th overall pick in the [[2026 NBA draft]].{{cite news |author=Marcus D. Smith |title=Sacramento Kings nab Emanuel Sharp in NBA Draft: Why you should love the grade|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/kings/2026/06/24/emanuel-sharp-sacramento-kings-nba-draft-grade/90684972007/|work=[[USA Today]]|date=June 24, 2026 |access-date=June 24, 2026}} At the time, there were three other Israeli players playing in the NBA: [[Deni Avdija]], [[Ben Saraf]], and [[ Danny Wolf]]. == National team == In 2019, at 15 years of age and between his freshman and sophomore years of high school, Sharp was a member of the [[Israel men's national under-16 basketball team|Israeli Under-16 national team]]. He competed in the [[FIBA U16 EuroBasket|FIBA U16 European Championship]], averaging 25 points per game.{{Cite web |date=2025-05-01 |title=Emanuel Christopher Sharp (Israel) |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/players/271529-emanuel-christopher-sharp |access-date=2025-05-01 |website=FIBA |language=en}} In 2025, Sharp said that he would play for Team Israel again, if the timing were right. ==Style of play== Analysts consider Sharp to be a high-IQ basketball player, with a very good quick release [[three-point shot]], excellent off-the-ball skills, known for making few [[Turnover (basketball)|turnover]]s, and being an excellent defender.[https://www.nba.com/draft/2026/prospects/emanuel-sharp "Emanuel Sharp,"] NBA.com. He was projected to specialize in shooting three-point shots and play top perimeter defense. Scouts compared his game to that of [[Tim Hardaway Jr.]], exhibiting toughness, effort, and reliability. ==Personal life== Sharp has Israeli, American and Canadian citizenship.{{Cite web |last=Murra |first=Michael |date=2025-02-20 |title=Israeli citizen playing key role in UH men’s basketball success
